title: ph service is no longer dispatchable through the CLI, though its Nginx/PM2/SSL provisioning scripts still ship
content:
**`ph service` is not dispatchable at 6.2.2-dev.45.** Before using anything below, know that the command cannot be reached through the CLI at all. It is absent from `phCliCommandNames` in `packages/shared/clis/command-names.ts` (whose 21 entries are `generate vetra connect build publish list l access-token registry-login inspect is migrate switchboard reactor login logout install add i uninstall remove`) and absent from `phCliCommands` in `clis/ph-cli/src/commands/ph-cli-commands.ts`. No alias resolves to it either.

The dispatch path is closed, not a passthrough. `clis/ph-cmd/src/cli.ts` forwards to ph-cli only when the name is in `phCliCommandNames`; otherwise it falls through to a cmd-ts `subcommands` tree (`clis/ph-cmd/src/commands/ph.ts`) whose members are `init`, `use`, `update`, `setup-globals`, `use-local` plus `phCliHelpCommands` — there is no dynamic import and no legacy-command loader, so cmd-ts simply errors on an unknown subcommand. Invoking the inner CLI directly does not help: `ph-cli service` fails the same way, because `phCli` is built solely from `phCliCommands`.

The implementation, however, still exists — orphaned, not deleted. `clis/ph-cli/src/commands/service.ts` is still present and still re-exported from the commands barrel (`index.ts`), its argument definitions still live at `packages/shared/clis/args/service.ts`, and `SERVICE_ACTIONS = ["start","stop","status","setup","restart"]` is still in `packages/shared/clis/constants.ts`. Only the registration is gone. Two things would break even if it were re-registered: the script paths in `service.ts` resolve relative to the bundled `dist/cli.mjs` and land outside the package, and the compile-time guard in `packages/shared/clis/args/help.ts` makes re-adding the name to `phCliCommandNames` a type error until a matching help command is added too.

**The oddity: the 6.2.x scaffold still generates the script.** `packages/codegen/src/templates/boilerplate/package.json.ts` emits `"service": "ph-cli service"` into every new project's `package.json`, alongside `"service-startup"` and `"service-unstartup"` entries that shell into `./node_modules/@powerhousedao/ph-cli/dist/scripts/service-startup.sh` — scripts which do not exist in the package at all. The same three entries are duplicated in `packageScripts` in `packages/shared/clis/constants.ts`. So `pnpm service` in a freshly generated project fails, and it fails with a CLI usage error rather than anything that hints why.

---

**What the wizard did (useful history, and the scripts are still on disk).** `service.ts` was only a thin `execSync` wrapper over two bash scripts under `clis/ph-cli/scripts/`, both still present and readable:

For VM/server deployment: `curl -fsSL https://apps.powerhouse.io/install | bash` installs Node 24, pnpm, and ph-cmd. Then `ph init <project>` and `ph service setup` ran `setup-environment`, an interactive, sudo-driven Ubuntu provisioning wizard configuring: (1) Package installation (ph install custom packages); (2) Database (local PostgreSQL with auto-generated password, or remote connection URL); (3) SSL (Let's Encrypt for production with domain prompts, or self-signed for dev); (4) Domain setup (connect and switchboard subdomains). The script installs and configures Nginx with WebSocket support, security headers, and static file serving — concretely `apt install postgresql nginx libnginx-mod-http-brotli-*`, rewriting `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf` via `sed` to enable gzip and brotli, writing a site file to `/etc/nginx/sites-available/`, symlinking it into `sites-enabled/`, removing the default site, and reloading via `systemctl`. Let's Encrypt is wired through `certbot --nginx --redirect` for both the Connect and Switchboard domains, with `certbot.timer` enabled for renewal. PM2 handles auto-restart on crash and boot startup — `manage-environment` runs `pm2 start "pnpm switchboard --port $SWITCHBOARD_PORT" --name "switchboard_<project>"` then `pm2 save`. Management was via `ph service start|stop|restart|status`, all of which mapped onto that same script. A PowerShell twin (`setup-environment.ps1`) covers Windows.

Because the scripts themselves are intact, the provisioning steps remain reproducible by hand — `bash node_modules/@powerhousedao/ph-cli/dist/scripts/setup-environment dev <projectName>` is the call `ph service setup` used to make. Treat that as an undocumented workaround, not a supported interface.

Provenance: registration absence verified in `packages/shared/clis/command-names.ts`, `clis/ph-cli/src/commands/ph-cli-commands.ts` and `packages/shared/clis/args/help.ts`; dispatch traced through `clis/ph-cmd/src/cli.ts` → `src/commands/ph.ts` and `clis/ph-cli/src/cli.ts` → `commands/ph-cli.ts`; wizard behaviour read from `clis/ph-cli/src/commands/service.ts` and `clis/ph-cli/scripts/{setup-environment,manage-environment}`; scaffold script confirmed in `packages/codegen/src/templates/boilerplate/package.json.ts`. All at 6.2.2-dev.45. The generated `clis/ph-cli/COMMANDS.md` has no Service section, confirming it is out of the live command tree; only the hand-maintained `README.md` and `COMMANDS-LEGACY.md` still document it.

_Source-verified 2026-08-13 against Powerhouse source at v6.2.2-dev.45._
description: ph service is in neither CLI registry, so it cannot be invoked; its implementation and Nginx/PM2/certbot scripts remain on disk, and the scaffold still emits a broken service npm script.
